item.wildroots.field_journal.desc: A naturalist's notes. Use to open.
wildroots.message.journal.received: You now carry a field journal.
wildroots.journal.hint.welcome.title: First Entry
wildroots.journal.hint.welcome: New species: %s. Plants from one spot are not alike. Sow seed from the best, and the offspring seem to take after them.
wildroots.journal.species.wild_carrot.se: White umbels, visible from far off. A single dark purple floret often sits at the centre of each. The root is thin and white, smells of carrot, and can be bitter. Roots from one patch differ noticeably.
wildroots.journal.species.wild_carrot.hi: Wild carrot grows across Europe and western Asia; in North America it's called Queen Anne's lace. Its root is white and tough. It seems people first valued it not for the root but for its fragrant leaves and seeds.
wildroots.journal.cultivar.eastern_carro: A root that isn't bitter, at least medium, and a little sweet. And coloured: yellow or purple.
wildroots.journal.cultivar.carrot.goal: A very large, sweet root with no bitterness. And orange, without a trace of purple.
wildroots.cultivar.eastern_carrot.note: Coloured carrots, purple and yellow, arose in Central Asia and Afghanistan. By around the 10th century Persian writers describe them as a vegetable, and by the 12th they had reached Spain.
wildroots.cultivar.carrot.note: Orange carrots spread through Europe in the 16th–17th centuries, and Dutch growers made them the standard. The story that they were bred to honour the House of Orange has no evidence behind it. The colour is beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A.
wildroots.journal.tool.field_journal: Everything found and bred is written here. A lost journal can be made again; the notes won't go anywhere.
wildroots.journal.tool.seed_pouch: A seed pouch. The packets inside never mix; each lies apart, and the last one put in is the first to come out.
wildroots.journal.hint.mother_plant: Pulling a ripe root gives two things: food, and a mother root. The mother root is the same plant with all its merits: planted, it flowers and sets seed. That's how selection goes: dig up, look, put the best back.
wildroots.journal.hint.plant_together: Plants of one kind pollinate each other when they grow close. A lone plant pollinates itself, which is said to bode ill.
wildroots.journal.hint.lone_plant.title: Alone in the Field
wildroots.journal.hint.lone_plant: This plant stands alone. If none of its kind flowers nearby, it will pollinate itself, and the offspring may come out weak.
wildroots.journal.hint.small_population: The bed is too small. A handful gives little to choose from, and rare traits slip away. A five-by-five bed is a good rule of thumb.
wildroots.journal.hint.select_quarter: Every fourth plant, the very best, is enough for seed. Choosier is faster, but it's easy to lose what hasn't shown itself yet.
wildroots.journal.hint.left_on_stalk: This wild plant flowered on its own, in its second year. Its seed is handy, but nobody ever saw the root. Selection blindfolded.
wildroots.journal.hint.root_ripe.title: The Root Is Ripe
wildroots.journal.hint.root_ripe: The root is ripe. It won't flower by itself: a carrot waits in the ground until it's dug up. Pull it and look, then eat it or plant the best back as a mother root.
wildroots.journal.hint.bitter.title: Bitter
wildroots.journal.hint.bitter: Bitter. But only some plants are, not all, which means the bitterness can be left behind next generation.
wildroots.journal.hint.yellow_root.title: A Yellow Root
wildroots.journal.hint.yellow_root: A yellow root! This may be how the eastern carrot began. The colour only shows when both parents pass it on; in the rest it can hide.
wildroots.journal.hint.orange_root.title: Orange
wildroots.journal.hint.orange_root: An orange root. Yellow alone isn't enough: it needs a second hidden trait, again from both parents. Guard it closely.
wildroots.journal.hint.purple_root.title: Purple
wildroots.journal.hint.purple_root: A purple root. This colour is strong: one parent is enough. But it masks both yellow and orange.
wildroots.journal.hint.bees.title: Bees
wildroots.journal.hint.bees: Bees hop from flower to flower, carrying pollen between plants. After their visits there's noticeably more seed.
wildroots.journal.hint.no_pollinators: Few seeds set. It seems nobody visited the flowers. Pollinators are needed; a wild bee nest nearby can be moved, if handled with a very gentle touch.
wildroots.journal.hint.inbreeding.title: Ailing
wildroots.journal.hint.inbreeding: Pale, short plants. Their parents were too closely related, or one plant pollinated itself. Fresh blood from another patch usually helps.
wildroots.journal.hint.hybrid_vigor: Two ailing lines gave sturdy offspring. Their weaknesses must have been different ones, and in the hybrid each covered for the other.
wildroots.journal.hint.stagnation.title: Stalled
wildroots.journal.hint.stagnation: Line "%s" has stalled: three generations without progress. The variety seems used up. Fresh stock is needed, from another biome, a village, a feral garden or an old cache. A plant breeder can tell where to look.
wildroots.journal.hint.missing_allele: Line "%s" seems to have no carriers of the trait it needs. The only way back is crossing with plants that have it.
wildroots.journal.hint.second_biome: Another patch, somewhere else, and these plants are strong in other ways. Brought together, they'll give more than either alone.
wildroots.journal.hint.climate.title: Out of Its Element
wildroots.journal.hint.climate: This plant is out of its climate: it grows, but grudgingly. Select the hardiest, or plant it somewhere more familiar.
wildroots.journal.hint.bone_meal.title: A Feed
wildroots.journal.hint.bone_meal: Bone meal hurries growth but doesn't improve the plant. The offspring won't change for it.
wildroots.journal.hint.unattended.title: Unattended
wildroots.journal.hint.unattended: Seed gathered unattended; who pollinated the flowers is anyone's guess. Best treat it as selfed.
wildroots.journal.hint.looks_like.title: Looks Like It, But…
wildroots.journal.hint.looks_like: This plant looks like %s. Looking like isn't being, though. Sow its seed and see whether the trait holds in the offspring.
wildroots.journal.hint.first_landrace: A landrace: a local variety. Not everything one could want, but no longer wild. Edible, not bitter, and its traits hold. The first farmers' gardens looked like this.
wildroots.journal.hint.first_cultivar: A cultivar. Every plant in it descends from that first one, where it all began.
wildroots.journal.hint.mutation.title: An Odd One
wildroots.journal.hint.mutation: An unusual plant that resembles neither parent. That's rare. Its seed is worth saving.
wildroots.journal.hint.carrier.title: Carrier
wildroots.journal.hint.carrier: The analyser found a carrier: the trait is there but hidden, invisible from outside. Cross two carriers and about a quarter of the offspring will show it.
wildroots.journal.hint.half_fixed.title: Not Yet Fixed
wildroots.journal.hint.half_fixed: The cultivar rests on one copy of the trait out of two. About a quarter of the offspring will lose it. To fix it, look for plants that got it from both parents.
wildroots.journal.hint.seed_pouch.title: The Pouch
wildroots.journal.hint.seed_pouch: Seed packets no longer spill across every pocket. In the pouch each lies apart, and the last one in is the first one out.
wildroots.journal.hint.vavilov.title: Vavilov
wildroots.journal.hint.vavilov: Nikolai Vavilov travelled five continents collecting the seeds of crops and their wild relatives. He looked for the places crops were born, where their variety runs richest. He named the apple forests near Almaty as the apple's homeland.
wildroots.message.journal.new_entry.body: Read it in the field journal

wildroots.journal.tool.hand_lens: The lens shows what the eye can't judge: taste, hardiness, how pollination went, whether a plant is ailing. Works on plants and on seed packets alike.
wildroots.message.needs_planting_materia: This won't take root. It needs planting material: a seed lot or a mother root.

block.wildroots.seed_analyser.desc: Heredity or luck? Uses bone meal.
wildroots.journal.tool.seed_analyser: The analyser answers the big question: heredity or luck? It shows what a plant will pass on, how much of it actually shows, and where its strength goes. It finds carriers of hidden traits. The seed comes out unharmed.

wildroots.journal.guide.start.title: Getting Started
wildroots.journal.guide.start.1: Wild plants grow in patches; wild carrot shows from far off by its white umbels. Pulled when ripe, it gives a root and a [[guide.mother_root|mother root]]. Pulled in seed, it gives a packet of seeds. Both go on farmland, close together: [[guide.pollination|neighbours]] pollinate each other.
wildroots.journal.guide.start.2: No two roots from one patch are quite alike: one thicker, one paler, one less bitter. Pigs and rabbits like them too: they follow, and they breed.
wildroots.journal.guide.journal.title: Using the Journal
wildroots.journal.guide.journal.1: Everything found and bred is written down here. The contents have two halves: the guide, which grows as new things turn up, and the records: species, cultivars, lines, notes. A green mark means something new. A lost journal is no loss: a new one opens the same pages.
wildroots.journal.guide.journal.2: Underlined words lead to other pages, and so do the items drawn on them. The star keeps a bookmark. Search looks only through pages already open. Arrow keys turn pages, Backspace goes back, Home opens the contents, Ctrl+F starts a search.
wildroots.journal.guide.seed_lot.title: Seed Lots
wildroots.journal.guide.seed_lot.1: A packet of seeds from one mother plant. Each seed grows into a plant of its own, and they rarely come up alike.
wildroots.journal.guide.seed_lot.2: A packet remembers where it came from: the species, the generation, the line's name if it has one, and who pollinated the mother. A dug-up sprout is another thing: planted again, it grows the very same plant. The [[guide.lens|lens]] tells more.
wildroots.journal.guide.stages.title: Growth Stages
wildroots.journal.guide.stages.2: Pulled young, a plant comes up as a sprout that can be planted again. A ripe root waits in the ground for as long as it takes: it will not flower by itself. Bone meal hurries a young plant; a ripe one won't take it. Only a planted [[guide.mother_root|mother root]] flowers and sets seed.
wildroots.journal.guide.mother_root.2: A mother root keeps every trait of its plant, so it is worth a look through the [[guide.lens|lens]] before deciding. Planted on farmland, it flowers; pulled before the seed is ripe, it simply comes back. It can be eaten too: the finer its grade, the quicker it goes down.
wildroots.journal.guide.cycle.title: The Biennial Cycle
wildroots.journal.guide.lens.title: The Hand Lens
wildroots.journal.guide.lens.1: A pane of glass, a copper ingot, a stick. Nothing rare: the lens is wanted from the very first days.
wildroots.journal.guide.lens.3: Put to a plant in the bed, the lens reads it. With seeds in the other hand, it reads the packet. In the inventory, carried on the cursor over seeds, a mother root or produce, it shows the [[guide.traits|bars]]. Seeds and mother roots need one click with the lens first.
wildroots.journal.guide.traits.title: Reading the Lens
wildroots.journal.guide.traits.intro: Five marks, five words. The more marks are filled, the stronger the trait.
wildroots.journal.guide.traits.how_to: Carry the lens on the cursor over seeds, a mother root or produce.
wildroots.journal.guide.traits.grade: Produce shows its grade instead: four marks, from coarse to choice.
wildroots.journal.guide.colors.title: Root Colour
wildroots.journal.guide.selection.title: Selection
wildroots.journal.guide.selection.1: Plants of one patch differ: one root bigger, another sweeter, a third not bitter at all. Their seed seems to take after them. So it goes: grow many, look closely, plant the best back, eat the rest. Generation by generation, the line drifts towards what was kept.
wildroots.journal.guide.selection.2: A bed of five by five is a good start; from fewer, there is little to choose. Every fourth plant, the very best, is enough for seed. Choosier is faster, but a trait that hasn't shown itself yet is easy to lose. The [[guide.traits|lens]] helps to choose.
wildroots.journal.guide.pollination.1: Flowers of one kind pollinate each other when they grow close and bloom together, and the seed carries traits of both parents. A plant with none of its kind in flower nearby pollinates itself, and its offspring may come out weak.
wildroots.journal.guide.pollination.2: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, and after their visits there is more seed. A wild nest can be moved, if handled with a very gentle touch.
wildroots.journal.guide.pollination.3: Few seeds in the heads: it seems nobody visited the flowers. A packet pulled by hand remembers its fathers. Seed gathered unattended, by a piston or by water, does not, and is best treated as selfed.
wildroots.journal.guide.inbreeding.title: Close Kin
wildroots.journal.guide.inbreeding.1: Pale, short plants: their parents were too close kin, or a plant pollinated itself. A line kept on a handful of plants slowly goes the same way. The [[guide.traits|lens]] marks such plants as ailing.
wildroots.journal.guide.inbreeding.2: Fresh blood helps: plants from another patch, better still from another biome, strong in other ways. Even two ailing lines can give sturdy offspring, if their weaknesses differ.
wildroots.journal.guide.cultivars.title: Landrace and Cultivar
wildroots.journal.guide.cultivars.1: A wild ancestor, then a landrace, then a cultivar. A landrace is a local variety: edible, not bitter, and its traits hold. A cultivar goes further. Looking like one is not being one: the lens judges by eye, and only the offspring tell for sure. The journal notes a new one as soon as it is sown.
wildroots.journal.guide.cultivars.2: What each cultivar should look like is in the records, under Cultivars.
wildroots.journal.guide.tool.field_journ: A book and a packet of seeds, any kind.
It works like a bundle: right-click the pouch onto a packet to put seeds in, and onto an empty slot to take the last one out. Only seeds go in. Its tooltip shows how full it is and what went in last.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.1: Two rows, two paths of one plant: grown from seed in front, a planted mother root behind.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.2: Pulled too early, a young plant comes up as a sprout. Planted again, it grows the same plant.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.3: The root is ripe and waits for as long as it takes. Pulled, it gives food and a mother root.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.4: Planted back, the mother root is the same plant, picking up where it stopped.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.5: Only the mother root flowers, and it needs pollinators. Pulled in flower, it gives the root back.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.6: The seed is ripe. Pulled by hand, it gives a packet that remembers its fathers.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_stages.st: Just sown. Pulled now, it comes up as a sprout to plant again.
Leaves only. Pulled now: a sprout that grows the same plant.
The root fills out under the leaves. Still too early to judge it.
Ripe, and waits until pulled: food and a mother root. A planted mother root gives only itself back.
Only a planted mother root flowers. Pulled now, it gives the root back.
The seed is ripe. Pulled, it gives a packet of seeds; the mother root is spent.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.1: A packet sown: each seed grows into a plant of its own, and no two are alike.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.2: The rosettes grow on until the roots are ripe.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.3: The roots are ripe and wait to be pulled; they grow no further. Some are bigger than others.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.4: The harvest gives food and a mother root from every plant. The best mother roots go back into the ground: they will parent the next generation.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.5: The mother roots flower. Bees carry pollen between neighbours.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.5.b: The mother roots flower. Bees, or a brush, carry pollen between neighbours.
wildroots.journal.scene.carrot_cycle.6: The seed is ripe: a packet that carries its fathers' traits too. And back to the start.
